proposed.explanation:
Comparison of the four companies on FY2025 vs FY2024 net-profit growth and trailing P/E (price ÷ FY2025 EPS):

• ETEL (Telecom Egypt): Net profit fell from 10,111,328,000 EGP to 578,063,000 EGP (−94.3 %), yet the reported EPS rose from 4.79 to 11.93 EGP. This internal contradiction makes the ETEL figures unreliable for a valuation call; I exclude it from the ranking.
• COMI (CIB): Net profit grew from 55,256,732,000 to 82,258,815,000 EGP (+48.9 %). EPS rose from 14.72 to 18.25 EGP. At 128.00 EGP the P/E is 7.0×.
• EFID (Edita): Net profit grew from 1,606,727,698 to 2,695,301,670 EGP (+67.8 %). EPS rose from 1.09 to 2.18 EGP. At 20.40 EGP the P/E is 9.4×.
• TMGH (Talaat Moustafa): Net profit grew from 12,769,517,325 to 18,201,981,482 EGP (+42.5 %). EPS rose from 4.38 to 6.98 EGP. At 82.50 EGP the P/E is 11.8×.

All three viable names show strong earnings growth at single-digit P/Es, implying PEG ratios well below 1. For a 7+ year growth mandate with medium risk tolerance, COMI offers the tightest margin of safety (P/E 7.0×) while still delivering nearly 49 % profit growth. The low multiple suggests the market is not fully pricing in the earnings trajectory, which is attractive for a patient, long-horizon investor.

Sizing: 312 shares × 128.00 EGP = 39,936 EGP. After the purchase the portfolio is 40,064 EGP cash + 39,936 EGP COMI = 80,000 EGP total, so COMI is 49.9 % of portfolio value, respecting the 50 % single-name cap. The remaining cash can be deployed later into a second or third position (e.g., EFID or TMGH) to build diversification.

Risks: Bank earnings are sensitive to interest-rate policy, credit-cycle shifts, and FX moves; a 48.9 % one-year jump may not be sustainable every year. The P/E of 7× could reflect a genuine market discount to Egyptian banks. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.

final.explanation:
Comparison of the four companies on FY2025 vs FY2024 net-profit growth and trailing P/E (price ÷ FY2025 EPS):

• ETEL (Telecom Egypt): Net profit grew from 10,111,328,000 EGP to 22,578,063,000 EGP (+123.3 %). EPS rose from 4.79 to 11.93 EGP/share. At 141.95 EGP the P/E is 11.9×. PEG ≈ 0.10.
• COMI (CIB): Net profit grew from 55,256,732,000 to 82,258,815,000 EGP (+48.9 %). EPS rose from 14.72 to 18.25 EGP. At 128.00 EGP the P/E is 7.0×. PEG ≈ 0.14.
• EFID (Edita): Net profit grew from 1,606,727,698 to 2,695,301,670 EGP (+67.8 %). EPS rose from 1.09 to 2.18 EGP. At 20.40 EGP the P/E is 9.4×. PEG ≈ 0.14.
• TMGH (Talaat Moustafa): Net profit grew from 12,769,517,325 to 18,201,981,482 EGP (+42.5 %). EPS rose from 4.38 to 6.98 EGP. At 82.50 EGP the P/E is 11.8×. PEG ≈ 0.28.

All four names show strong earnings growth. ETEL stands out with the highest profit growth (+123 %) and the best PEG ratio (≈0.10), meaning the market is pricing in very little of that growth at an 11.9× multiple. For a 7+ year growth mandate, a telecom operator with recurring subscription revenue and a 123 % earnings jump offers a compelling entry point. The defensive, regulated nature of telecom also suits a medium risk tolerance better than a pure-play bank or a diversified holding company.

Sizing: 281 shares × 141.95 EGP = 39,887.95 EGP. After the purchase the portfolio is 40,112.05 EGP cash + 39,887.95 EGP ETEL = 80,000 EGP total, so ETEL is 49.9 % of portfolio value, respecting the 50 % single-name cap. The remaining cash can be deployed later into a second position (e.g., COMI or EFID) to build diversification.

Risks: A 123 % one-year profit jump may include one-off items or a low base and is unlikely to repeat at the same rate; forward P/E could be higher if earnings normalise. Telecom is capital-intensive and regulated, limiting upside in a low-growth macro environment. The 11.9× P/E, while reasonable for the growth, is not as cheap as COMI's 7×, so there is less margin of safety on a pure multiple basis. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
